correctness.rationale: The first-step linear system uses weights 1/(n d_receiver), 1/(n d_sender) and 1/(2|E|) for VM, IP and LD respectively. The diagonal retains all no-op attempts and the fair-i.i.d. average divides by 2^n, including the absorbing initial states with zero time. A connected graph admits a positive-probability sequence of copies down a spanning tree that makes any configuration monochromatic, so the transient resolvent exists. At n<=2 there is no eligible nonedge; at n=3 only the path-to-triangle case occurs. At n=4 the trees give one star and two path orbits, the unicyclic paw and C4 give one orbit each, and the diamond gives the sole five-edge orbit. A separately written exact-rational solver reproduced the entire table: n=3 differences in VM/LD/IP order are (0,-1/2,-3/2); the four-vertex positive counts are 2/0/1, with all six LD differences negative. It recovered the VM star-to-paw 155/208, LD star-to-paw -1/17 and IP square-to-diamond 35/88, as well as five-vertex LD star means 613/48 before and 693195/52592 after, yielding 32327/78888. These establish sharp boundaries 4,5,4 in VM/LD/IP order. The frozen program was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: Witness only at five vertices, not a complete order-five classification. The calculation is for attempts, not discordant-only updates or fixed per-edge total clocks across different graphs.
